issues.body: Step C prescribes `python3 scripts/ledger-invariant.py` against a fresh checkout of the rewritten branch. The shipped program requires a positional `root` unless `--self-test` is used, so that exact invocation exits in argparse before validating anything. In addition, the ledger branch is deliberately data-only and its allowlist excludes `scripts/`; if the operator enters the fresh ledger checkout, the named script is absent. This is not merely cosmetic: the document calls §5 executable today, and this is its pre-resume tree-shape check.
issues.fix_hint: Give an exact command that runs the validator from a trusted checkout of the code branch while passing the separate rewritten-ledger checkout as its positional root, for example `python3 <registry-checkout>/scripts/ledger-invariant.py <rewritten-ledger-checkout>`. State which reviewed code SHA supplies the validator and keep both paths distinct so the operator cannot accidentally execute code from the rewritten data branch or validate the wrong repository.
issues.title: The prescribed ledger-invariant post-check cannot run as written

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-2 finding is resolved: step C now explicitly forbids the mutating `--claim` and bare `groom.py` paths and replaces them with SHA-pinned, read-only checks. However, the first replacement post-check is not executable as written. `ledger-invariant.py` requires a checkout-root positional argument, and the rewritten data-only checkout cannot itself contain `scripts/ledger-invariant.py`. Because this command is the runbook's tree-shape gate before writers resume, the maintenance procedure remains incomplete. Under the required progress scale this is regressing: the prior finding was fixed, but a new major finding remains.
